_scope_note: Runtime fixtures for the recurring-defect bullet under Fix Completeness in templates/rules/code-quality.md (a defect class that returns gets a guard, when the guard stays inside the request's correctness blast radius), issue #5410 (required behavioral fixture 7, structural recurrence). recurring-defect-adds-guard and recurring-defect-explanation-is-not-a-guard enable read and write tools, start the edit in source (dates.py, which matches the rule's `**/*.py` `paths:` glob, so a source-only repair loads the rule), and assert the files the agent writes (a fix in dates.py and a tests/test_dates.py). recurring-defect-ablated-no-rule is the ablated control of recurring-defect-adds-guard: the same prompt, files, and assertions with the rule not installed. The harness maps the `write` tool to Claude Edit, which cannot create files (issue #6710), so on the Claude harness the tests/test_dates.py file_regex reflects tool wiring as much as behavior until #6710 lands. Comparing the two live shows whether the rule changes behavior only once that is fixed. In a dry run the controls only prove each assertion can pass and fail. first-occurrence-targeted-fix-only sets `tools: []` and grades only the final message, so it measures what the agent REPORTS, not what it writes. Each fixture pairs regex/not_regex/file assertions with a `semantic` assertion graded by scripts/eval/_runtime_grader.py. The regex assertions are NOT the semantic authority: a response can name a guard in words no pattern lists, which the semantic assertion grades. Dry run: uv run python scripts/eval/eval_runtime_parity.py --fixtures tests/evals/structural-recurrence-runtime-fixtures.json --dry-run. Live results for this corpus are recorded in PR #6687.

def parse_stamp(value: str) -> int:
